sources: Tax Foundation, State Individual Income Tax Rates and Brackets, 2025 (taxfoundation.org/data/all/state/state-income-tax-rates/)

State revenue department and legislative sources for 2025 law changes: GA HB 111, ID HB 40, UT HB 106, MD HB 352 (Comptroller tax alert), WI 2025 Act 15 (WI DOR), VA HB 1600 (VA Dept. of Taxation), WV Code 11-21-4i, OH Rev. Code 5747.02, SC DOR
California FTB 2025 tax rate schedules (via CalCPA/TaxAct)
US Dept. of Labor, Wage and Hour Division, state minimum wage tables, plus Jan 1, 2025 state increase summaries
US Census Bureau, American Community Survey 2024 1-year estimates, median household income (table B19013 / S1901, via CRS report R48943)
_meta.notes: Single filers only. Brackets are [upper bound of taxable income, rate] with null for the top bracket, applied after standard_deduction_single. Where a state uses personal exemptions, the exemption is added into standard_deduction_single. Personal credits are not modeled and are listed in note. Where a state has a 0% first bracket, it is either a 0.0 bracket or folded into the deduction for flat states (ID, MS). Federal-conforming deductions use the $15,000 figure Tax Foundation published; the 2025 federal law (OBBBA) raised the federal amount to $15,750 and conforming states may follow it. median_household_income is the ACS 2024 1-year estimate, the latest state-level release available at compile time (2025 1-year estimates not yet found). min_wage is the general statewide rate in effect on Jan 1, 2025 (federal $7.25 where there is no higher state rate). Mid-year changes are listed in note. local_income_tax is true where most residents pay a city, county or school income tax (IN, KY, MD, MI cities, NY/NYC, OH, PA). These are estimates, not filing-grade calculations.

states.name: Alabama
states.note: Deduction = $1,500 personal exemption + $2,500 standard deduction (the $3,000 single standard deduction phases down to $2,500 above about $33,000 AGI). Federal income tax paid is deductible on the AL return (not modeled). A few cities (Birmingham, Bessemer, Gadsden etc.) levy occupational taxes. No state minimum wage; federal $7.25 applies.

states.name: Alaska
states.note: No state income tax. Minimum wage $11.91 from Jan 1, 2025, rising to $13.00 on July 1, 2025.

states.name: Arizona
states.note: Flat 2.5%. Arizona's standard deduction matches the federal amount ($15,000 as published for 2025; $15,750 if Arizona adopts the 2025 federal increase).

states.name: Arkansas
states.note: Simplified to the high-income schedule (2% then 3.9% top rate); lower-income filers use separate tables with lower tax. Plus a $29 personal tax credit (not modeled).

states.name: California
states.note: 2025 brackets and $5,706 standard deduction. An extra 1% Mental Health Services Tax applies to taxable income over $1M (13.3% top). Also a $153 single personal exemption credit (not modeled). Employees pay ~1.2% SDI with no wage cap (not an income tax).

states.name: Colorado
states.note: Flat 4.4%, starting from federal taxable income, so the deduction is the federal standard deduction ($15,000 pre-OBBBA; $15,750 if the state follows the 2025 federal increase). Denver, Aurora, Glendale, Greenwood Village and Sheridan levy small monthly occupational privilege taxes (not modeled).

states.name: Connecticut
states.note: No standard deduction. The $15,000 personal exemption phases out between $30,000 and $44,000 AGI, so it is 0 for a typical earner. The 2% bracket benefit is recaptured at higher incomes and there is a small property-tax/personal credit (not modeled).

states.name: Delaware
states.note: Also a $110 personal credit (not modeled). Wilmington levies a 1.25% earned income tax on residents and workers.

states.name: District of Columbia
states.note: Standard deduction tied to the federal amount ($15,000). Minimum wage $17.50 from Jan 1, 2025; $17.95 from July 1, 2025.

states.name: Florida
states.note: No state income tax. Minimum wage $13.00 (since Sept 30, 2024), rising to $14.00 on Sept 30, 2025.

states.name: Georgia
states.note: Flat 5.19% for 2025 (cut from 5.39% retroactively by HB 111, 2025). $12,000 single standard deduction. State minimum wage is $5.15 but the federal $7.25 applies to nearly all workers.

states.name: Hawaii
states.note: Deduction = $4,400 standard deduction + $1,144 personal exemption. Brackets widened in 2025 under Act 46 (2024).

states.name: Idaho
states.note: Flat 5.3% for 2025 (cut from 5.695% by HB 40, 2025). Idaho taxes the first $4,811 of taxable income at 0%; that zero bracket is folded into the deduction ($15,000 federal standard deduction + $4,811). Also a $155 grocery credit (not modeled).

states.name: Illinois
states.note: Flat 4.95%. Deduction is the $2,850 personal exemption (no standard deduction). Chicago minimum wage is higher.

states.name: Indiana
states.note: Flat 3.0% for 2025. Deduction is the $1,000 personal exemption. All 92 counties levy a local income tax (roughly 0.5% to 3.4%, about 1.5% to 2% typical).

states.name: Iowa
states.note: Newly flat 3.8% in 2025. Iowa starts from federal taxable income, so the deduction is the federal standard deduction ($15,000 pre-OBBBA; $15,750 if the state follows the 2025 federal increase). $40 personal credit (not modeled). Many school districts add a surtax on state tax (a few percent of the state tax).

states.name: Kansas
states.note: Two brackets after the 2024 reform. Deduction = $3,605 standard deduction + $9,160 personal exemption.

states.name: Kentucky
states.note: Flat 4.0% for 2025 (3.5% in 2026). Most cities and many counties levy occupational license taxes on wages (often 1% to 2.5%; Louisville about 2.2%).

states.name: Louisiana
states.note: Newly flat 3.0% in 2025 with a $12,500 standard deduction (replacing the old personal exemption).

states.name: Maine
states.note: Deduction = $15,000 standard deduction + $5,150 personal exemption; both phase out at high incomes.

states.name: Maryland
states.note: 2025 changes (HB 352, retroactive to Jan 1, 2025): new 6.25% and 6.5% top brackets and a flat $3,350 standard deduction. Deduction = $3,350 + $3,200 personal exemption. All counties and Baltimore City add a local income tax of 2.25% to 3.3%.

states.name: Massachusetts
states.note: 5% flat rate plus a 4% surtax on income over $1,083,150 (2025). Deduction is the $4,400 personal exemption (no standard deduction).

states.name: Michigan
states.note: Flat 4.25%. Deduction is the $5,800 personal exemption. 24 cities levy income tax (Detroit 2.4% for residents; most others 1%). Minimum wage $10.56 on Jan 1, 2025, rising to $12.48 on Feb 21, 2025.

states.name: Minnesota
states.note: 2025 brackets and $14,950 standard deduction. Minneapolis and St. Paul minimum wages are higher.

states.name: Mississippi
states.note: Flat 4.4% for 2025 on income over $10,000. Deduction = $2,300 standard deduction + $6,000 personal exemption + the $10,000 zero bracket folded in. No state minimum wage; federal $7.25 applies.

states.name: Missouri
states.note: Top rate 4.7% for 2025. Missouri's standard deduction equals the federal amount ($15,000 as published; $15,750 after the 2025 federal increase). Kansas City and St. Louis levy a 1% earnings tax on residents and workers. Minimum wage $13.75 from Jan 1, 2025 (Proposition A).

states.name: Montana
states.note: Montana starts from federal taxable income, so the deduction is the federal standard deduction ($15,000 as published for 2025).

states.name: Nebraska
states.note: Top rate cut to 5.2% for 2025 (falling to 3.99% by 2027). Also a $171 personal exemption credit (not modeled).

states.name: Nevada
states.note: No state income tax.

states.name: New Hampshire
states.note: No tax on wages. The interest and dividends tax was repealed starting with 2025, so there is no personal income tax in 2025. No state minimum wage beyond the federal $7.25.

states.name: New Jersey
states.note: Deduction is the $1,000 personal exemption (no standard deduction). Newark levies a 1% payroll tax on employers, not employees. Minimum wage $15.49 for employers with 6+ employees.

states.name: New Mexico
states.note: New bracket structure from 2025 (HB 252). Deduction is the federal standard deduction ($15,000 as published).

states.name: New York
states.note: New York City residents also pay 3.078% to 3.876% city income tax, and Yonkers residents a surcharge. Minimum wage $15.50 upstate; $16.50 in NYC, Long Island and Westchester.

states.name: North Carolina
states.note: Flat 4.25% for 2025 (3.99% in 2026). $12,750 single standard deduction.

states.name: North Dakota
states.note: Starts from federal taxable income, so the deduction is the federal standard deduction ($15,000 pre-OBBBA; $15,750 if the state follows the 2025 federal increase). The first $48,475 of taxable income is taxed at 0%.

states.name: Ohio
states.note: Ohio's 2025 schedule is 0% up to $26,050, then $342 + 2.75% over $26,050, then 3.125% over $100,000 (2.75% flat from 2026). The 0% bracket is shown as $13,614 so the fixed $342 is reproduced for incomes above $26,050. Deduction is the $2,150 personal exemption (for $40k-$80k income). Most cities and many school districts levy income tax (often 1.5% to 2.5%).

states.name: Oklahoma
states.note: Deduction = $6,350 standard deduction + $1,000 personal exemption. Top rate falls to 4.5% in 2026.

states.name: Oregon
states.note: Also a personal exemption credit of about $250 (not modeled). Portland-area residents with income over $125,000 pay Metro SHS (1%) and Multnomah County Preschool for All (1.5% and up) taxes. Minimum wage $14.70 standard; $15.05 from July 1, 2025 (Portland metro higher).

states.name: Pennsylvania
states.note: Flat 3.07% with no standard deduction or personal exemption. Nearly all municipalities and school districts levy an earned income tax (often about 1%; Philadelphia's wage tax is about 3.75% for residents).

states.name: Rhode Island
states.note: Deduction = $10,900 standard deduction + $5,100 personal exemption; both phase out at high incomes.

states.name: South Carolina
states.note: Top rate 6.0% for 2025 (down from 6.2%). Starts from federal taxable income, so the deduction is the federal standard deduction ($15,000 pre-OBBBA; $15,750 if the state follows the 2025 federal increase). No state minimum wage; federal $7.25 applies.

states.name: South Dakota
states.note: No state income tax.

states.name: Tennessee
states.note: No state income tax (Hall tax on investment income fully repealed in 2021). No state minimum wage; federal $7.25 applies.

states.name: Texas
states.note: No state income tax.

states.name: Utah
states.note: Flat 4.5% for 2025 (cut from 4.55% by HB 106, 2025). No standard deduction: Utah gives a taxpayer credit of 6% of the federal standard deduction (about $900), phased out by 1.3% of income above roughly $18,000, so it is worth a few hundred dollars at typical incomes (not modeled).

states.name: Vermont
states.note: Deduction = $7,400 standard deduction + $5,100 personal exemption.

states.name: Virginia
states.note: Deduction = $8,750 standard deduction (raised for 2025-2026 by HB 1600) + $930 personal exemption.

states.name: Washington
states.note: No tax on wages. A 7% tax applies to long-term capital gains over about $270,000 (9.9% over $1M from 2025). Employees pay WA Cares (0.58%) and paid-leave premiums (not income taxes).

states.name: West Virginia
states.note: 2025 rates after a 4% trigger cut plus an extra 2% cut (top 4.82%). Deduction is the $2,000 personal exemption (no standard deduction). Some cities (e.g. Charleston, Huntington) levy flat weekly user fees (not modeled).

states.name: Wisconsin
states.note: 2025 Act 15 widened the 4.4% bracket to $50,480. Wisconsin's sliding-scale standard deduction ($13,560 maximum) shrinks as income rises. $9,348 is the deduction (about $8,648) plus the $700 exemption for a single filer earning about $60,000. Lower earners get more and those above about $132,000 get none.

states.name: Wyoming
states.note: No state income tax. State minimum wage is $5.15 but the federal $7.25 applies to nearly all workers.
